name: corporate_action_arb_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: On ex-dividend/ex-bonus/ex-split dates, NSE adjusts the previous close by the corporate action amount, but the market's opening price frequently overshoots or undershoots this theoretical adjusted price. For dividends, stocks often open at a smaller discount than the dividend amount (partial adjustment) — especially for special dividends — creating a long opportunity. For stock splits, the post-split price often overshoots the theoretical adjustment due to retail 'cheap stock' bias. The inefficiency exists because: (1) many retail traders don't correctly compute the adjusted price, (2) limit orders from the previous day carry over unadjusted, creating temporary mispricing, (3) the adjustment is mechanical but the market's reaction is behavioral.
universe: All NSE stocks with corporate actions (dividend, split, bonus)
stock_filter: Ex-date today, ADV > ₹10 crore, corporate action value > 1% of stock price

other: theoretical adjusted price (prev_close - dividend, or prev_close / split_ratio)

indicators.name: theoretical_adjusted_price
indicators.formula: prev_close - dividend_amount (for dividends) OR prev_close / split_ratio (for splits) OR prev_close * shares_old / shares_new (for bonus)

conditions: adjustment_error_bps < -20 (stock opened too low relative to theoretical — overadjusted)
adjustment_error_bps > 20 (stock opened too high — underadjusted, especially for splits)

entry.entry_price: market order within first 15 min of detecting mispricing

exit.target: adjustment_error_bps converges to ±5 bps (near fair value)
exit.stop_loss: adjustment_error_bps extends to ±50 bps (mispricing is genuine, not noise)
exit.time_stop: exit by 11:00 IST (adjustment should complete by then)
exit.signal_exit: stock trades through theoretical_adjusted_price and keeps going (overshoot in other direction)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L per trade, reduce for stocks with ADV < ₹20 crore

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter (corporate action adjustment is independent of volatility regime)
filters.trend_filter: skip if NIFTY 50 is moving > 1% in first 30 min (market move dominates adjustment effect)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 15 bps (ex-date spreads can be wider)
filters.event_filter: only trade on ex-dates with corporate action value > 1% of stock price (material)
other_filters: skip bonus issues < 1:5 (too small to create meaningful mispricing)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — corporate action adjustment errors are driven by behavioral biases and mechanical order book issues that are structural. As long as corporate actions occur, the signal persists.

weaknesses: Corporate actions are infrequent for any single stock, and material actions (>1% of price) are rarer still. The strategy may generate only 5-10 trades per month.
For dividends, the stock may legitimately open below theoretical adjustment if the market is pricing in reduced future earnings or if it's an unsustainable special dividend.
The theoretical adjusted price computation can be complex for combined actions (e.g., dividend + bonus on same date) leading to calculation errors.
prior_art: Elton & Gruber (1970) 'Marginal Stockholder Tax Rates and the Clientele Effect' — original ex-dividend pricing research. Frank & Jagannathan (1998) 'Why Do Stock Prices Drop by Less Than the Value of the Dividend?'. In India, Mishra (2005) studies ex-dividend behavior in NSE.
notes: Critical: verify the corporate action type and amount from NSE's corporate action calendar at least one day before ex-date. Compute theoretical_adjusted_price before market open. Monitor F&O adjustment circulars for stocks in F&O segment — NSE adjusts strike prices and lot sizes, which can affect option chain pricing.
